era: 1928-1967 : 阿根廷—古巴革命—刚果与玻利维亚（医学青年—游击战士—革命输出者）
era_en: 1928-1967 : Argentina - Cuban Revolution - Congo and Bolivia (medical student - guerrilla commander - exporter of revolution)
school: 格瓦拉主义 (Guevarismo) / 游击中心论 (focalism)
historical_significance: 埃内斯托·切·格瓦拉（1928-1967），阿根廷出生的马克思主义革命家、医师，古巴革命的核心指挥者之一，革命胜利后任古巴国家银行行长与工业部长。他提出并实践了游击中心论（foco）：不等客观条件成熟而以小股精锐点燃武装斗争，让行动本身创造群众条件；他与苏联『物质刺激』路线公开分野，主张以道德激励铸造『社会主义新人』。1965年他辞去一切职务、放弃国籍，先后远征刚果与玻利维亚，1967年10月在玻利维亚被俘就义。其遗容照片意外成为全球传播最广的革命符号。他的方法论——焦点点火、道德动员、亲身远征、日记自审、终局抉择——构成理想主义行动者在现实约束下运作的完整思维模式体系，其失败与成功同样具有方法论价值。
historical_significance_en: Ernesto 'Che' Guevara (1928-1967), Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary and physician, a core commander of the Cuban Revolution and later President of Cuba's National Bank and Minister of Industries. He advanced and practiced focalism (foco): rather than waiting for objective conditions, a small elite band ignites armed struggle, with action itself creating the popular conditions; he openly split with the Soviet 'material incentives' line, arguing that moral incentives forge the 'socialist new man.' In 1965 he resigned every post and renounced his citizenship, leading expeditions to the Congo and then Bolivia, where he was captured and executed in October 1967. Photographs of his remains unexpectedly became the most widely circulated revolutionary image in the world. His methodology—foco ignition, moral mobilization, personal expedition, diary self-audit, and endgame choice—forms a complete system of thinking modes for the idealist actor operating under real constraints, with his failures carrying as much methodological value as his successes.
unique_thinking: 用最小的火种去测试最大的信念：条件不成熟就把自己当作条件——先以医生之眼看见具体痛苦，再以战士之身把痛苦转译为行动，并随时准备把个人全部押上，让理想以自己为最后的载体。
unique_thinking_en: Test the largest conviction with the smallest spark: when conditions are unripe, make yourself the condition—see concrete suffering first with a physician's eyes, then translate it into action as a combatant, ready at any moment to stake everything personal so the ideal has one last carrier: himself.
civilization_zh: 拉丁美洲文明（南美—加勒比—拉美国际主义）
civilization_en: Latin American civilization (South America - Caribbean - pan-Latin American internationalism)
roles_zh: 古巴革命游击队指挥官
roles_en: President of the National Bank of Cuba
Guerrilla commander of the Cuban Revolution
key_works: 《古巴的社会主义与人》(El socialismo y el hombre en Cuba, 1965)

modes.domain_zh: 不等待客观条件成熟才发动，而是主动投入一支小而精的游击队（foco）在偏远山区点燃焦点，让武装斗争本身去创造革命的主观条件——群众不是先被说服再跟随，而是在看见火种燃烧的过程中被唤醒
modes.domain_en: Rather than waiting for objective conditions to ripen, commit a small, elite guerrilla band (a foco) to a remote mountain zone and let armed struggle itself manufacture the subjective conditions of revolution—the people are not persuaded first and then mobilized, but awakened by watching the spark burn
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉对二十世纪左翼最大的方法论挑战是推翻了正统马克思主义的阶段论：不必先有发达资本主义、先有觉悟的无产阶级、先有党的漫长经营，一支三四十人的游击队就可以成为『革命的先锋队中的先锋队』。其逻辑有三层：其一，条件论反转——古巴经验证明，在拉丁美洲近乎一切国家，客观条件已经成熟到可以发动武装斗争，缺的从来不是条件而是点火的人；主观条件（群众觉悟、组织网络）恰恰是武装斗争本身的产物而非前提。其二，地理学即战略学——选择马埃斯特腊山这样的边缘地带：国家权力稀薄、地形利于防御、农民积怨深厚，使极小的武装获得不成比例的生存能力。其三，行动即宣传——游击队每打一次伏击、每救治一个农民，都在完成一次比报纸小册子有效的动员。深意在于：他把革命的起点从『说服多数』改为『展示可能』，用极小成本的示范效应撬动不动的大众。代价同样写在古巴经验里：在无山区、无农民基础、国家机器强大的环境里，foco论几乎必然失败——他在玻利维亚付出了生命。现代对应物是最小可行产品、社会运动的可见性事件设计与组织变革中的试点点火。
modes.definition_en: Guevara's biggest methodological challenge to twentieth-century leftism was overturning orthodox Marxist stage theory: no need for advanced capitalism, an awakened proletariat, or decades of party groundwork first—a guerrilla band of thirty or forty can itself be 'the vanguard of the vanguard of revolution.' The logic has three layers. First, the reversal of the conditions argument: the Cuban experience proved that in nearly every Latin American country the objective conditions were already ripe for armed struggle; what was missing was never the conditions but the people willing to light the fire—subjective conditions (popular consciousness, organizational networks) are the product of armed struggle, not its precondition. Second, geography is strategy: choose marginal terrain like the Sierra Maestra—thin state presence, defensible topography, deep peasant grievance, corridors for maneuver—so a tiny force gains disproportionate survivability. Third, action is propaganda: every ambush, every barracks burned, every campesino treated by the column's doctor accomplished mobilization more effective than any pamphlet; fire creates the fire. The deeper point: he moved the starting point of revolution from 'persuading the majority' to 'demonstrating possibility,' levering an immovable majority with a minimal-cost demonstration. The cost is equally written into the record: in environments without mountains, without a peasant base, with a strong state (the Bolivian lowlands), foco theory fails almost inevitably—and there he paid with his life. Modern analogues: minimum viable products in lean startups, visibility-event design in social movements, and pilot ignition in organizational change.
modes.source_chapter: 《游击战》(Guerra de guerrillas, 1960)；古巴革命马埃斯特腊山时期 (1956-1958)；《革命战争随笔》(1963)
modes.key_quote_zh: 不要等条件的链条上每一环都成熟——第一个敢于点火的人，本身就是被缺少的那一环。
modes.key_quote_en: Do not wait for every link in the chain of conditions to ripen—the one who dares to light the fire is himself the missing link.
process_zh: 评估条件梯度：判断目标环境是否具备焦点生存的最低配（可藏身地形、被排斥的农村人群、政权控制薄弱带），缺一即需重新选址或放弃
小队点火：以数十人规模的精干队伍进驻选定区域，先求生存不求扩张，用纪律与医疗等民生行为积累当地信任
行动造浪：以小规模可复制的军事胜利制造心理浪潮，每一次成功都同步转化为招募、补给与情报网络
焦点扩散：当第一个焦点稳定后裂变出多个焦点互相呼应，从山区游击走向城镇与总罢工，把军事胜利转译为政权更替
process_en: Assess the conditions gradient: judge whether the target environment has the minimum viable configuration for foco survival—hidable terrain, an excluded rural population, thin state control; if any is absent, relocate or abandon
Ignite with a small team: insert a lean column of a few dozen; seek survival first, not expansion, accumulating local trust through discipline and services like medical care
Make waves with action: use small, replicable military successes to create psychological ripples, converting each into recruitment, supply, and intelligence networks in real time

Diffuse the foco: once the first focus stabilizes, split into mutually reinforcing foci, moving from mountain guerrilla war to urban strikes and general insurrection, translating military victory into regime change
representative_cases_zh: 1956年格拉玛号登陆：82人出发、登陆后仅剩十余人在马埃斯特腊山站稳——三年后这粒火种发展成数千人的起义军并推翻巴蒂斯塔政权，成为foco论的经典实证
马埃斯特腊山的『第七号法令』：起义军在控制区内豁免农民地租、建立学校与无线电电台——把根据地做成『另一个国家』的样板，农民从旁观者变为参与者
圣克拉拉战役（1958年末）：格瓦拉用一列装甲列车伏击战拿下战略重镇，几天后哈瓦那不战而落——焦点已扩散到『每一座城市都在燃烧』的临界点
反例警示：1966-67年玻利维亚尼亚卡瓦苏河谷——无农民基础、无可用山区、当地共产党拒绝合作，foco被政府军与CIA合围歼灭，格瓦拉被俘处决；条件缺位时强行点火等于自焚
representative_cases_en: The Granma landing, 1956: 82 set out; barely a dozen held firm in the Sierra Maestra after landing—three years later that spark grew into an army of thousands that toppled Batista, the classic empirical vindication of foco theory

Decree No. 7 in the Sierra Maestra: the rebels exempted campesinos from rent in zones under their control and built schools and a radio station—making the base area a model of 'another country,' turning peasants from bystanders into participants

The Battle of Santa Clara, late 1958: Guevara's ambush of an armored train took the strategic hub; Havana fell days later without a fight—the foco had spread to the tipping point where 'every city was burning'

Counter-case: the Ñancahuazú valley, Bolivia, 1966-67—no peasant base, no usable mountains, the local communist party refusing cooperation; the foco was encircled and annihilated by government forces with CIA support, and Guevara was captured and executed. Forcing ignition without conditions is self-immolation
modern_applications_zh: 精益创业：不写三年商业计划，用最小可行产品在真实市场里『打一场伏击』，让用户行为而非调查报告告诉你条件是否成熟
社会创新：推动公共议题时先做一个小而可见的示范点（一间样板社区图书馆、一条改造街道），用事实影像与可参观性完成说服
组织变革：新流程先在一个高意愿小团队里跑通，让内部参观与口碑代替自上而下的推行文件
个人转型：不必等『准备完全』才开始，选择自己人生中的『马埃斯特腊山』——一个低风险高支持的切入点先站住脚
modern_applications_en: Lean startup: skip the three-year business plan; fight one ambush with a minimum viable product in the real market, and let user behavior—not survey reports—tell you whether conditions are ripe

Social innovation: when advancing a public cause, build one small, visible demonstration first (a model community library, one reclaimed street) and let facts, images, and visitability do the persuading
Organizational change: run a new process through one willing small team, and let internal tours and word of mouth replace top-down rollout memos
Personal transformation: do not wait until you are 'fully ready'; choose your own Sierra Maestra—a low-risk, high-support entry point—and hold it first
representative_figures: 丹尼斯·里维拉·卡米洛·西恩富戈斯

modes.domain_zh: 制度变革若无人的改变终将回潮，因此把培养『社会主义新人』当作与经济制度同等重要的工程：用道德激励替代物质刺激，用劳动中的自我实现重塑工作意义，让新制度有新人格托底
modes.domain_en: Institutional change without a change in people will always regress; therefore raise the 'socialist new man' as an engineering project as important as the economic system itself: replace material incentives with moral ones, remake the meaning of work as self-realization in labor, and give the new institution a new personality to rest upon
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉在工业部与国家银行任上的核心争论，是与苏联模式『物质刺激』路线的公开分歧。他坚持：如果用资本主义时代的利己动机去运转社会主义制度，制度会在运转中把旧人再生产出来，最终吃掉制度本身。方法有三：其一，道德激励制度化——义务劳动（周五志愿劳动）、『社会主义劳动竞赛』、突击队荣誉体系，把『为共同体劳动』变成有仪式、有荣誉、有排行榜的公共生活，而非靠禁欲说教维持。其二，劳动意义的重写——他反复论证工作应是『自我实现的场所』：人在改造自然的同时改造自己，劳动从谋生手段变成人格完成的途径，这是他《论社会主义新人》一文的核心。其三，以身作则的『新人样板』——他自己白天当部长、周日砍甘蔗，子女不许特权，海外作战不领分文；用一把『我做得到』的尺子丈量整个官僚层。深意在于：他把文化改造放在与制度改造同等的位置，预见了苏联式倒退的根因——制度先进而人格依旧。代价是被批评为道德理想主义：当物质匮乏真实存在时，纯道德动员可持续性有限，且易滑向对异见者不宽容。现代对应物是使命驱动型组织、志愿体系设计与企业文化中的『创始人以身作则』。
modes.definition_en: The central argument of Guevara's tenure at the Ministry of Industries and the National Bank was his open split with the Soviet 'material incentives' line. He insisted: run a socialist system with the self-interested motives of the capitalist era, and the system will reproduce old men in its gears until it devours itself. The method has three parts. First, institutionalizing moral incentives: voluntary labor (Friday volunteer brigades), socialist emulation campaigns, and honor systems for shock brigades turn 'working for the community' into public life with ritual, honor, and leaderboards, rather than sustaining it by ascetic preaching. Second, rewriting the meaning of work: he argued repeatedly that work should be the site of self-realization—humans remake themselves in remaking nature, labor passing from means of survival to vehicle of personal completion, the core of his essay 'Socialism and Man in Cuba.' Third, modeling the new man by example: he served as minister by day, cut cane on Sundays, allowed his children no privilege, and drew no pay for foreign service; he measured the whole bureaucracy with the ruler of 'I can do it.' The deeper point: he placed cultural transformation on par with institutional transformation, foreseeing the root cause of Soviet-style regression—an advanced system with unreformed personalities. The cost: criticized as moral idealism; where material scarcity is real, purely moral mobilization has limited staying power and slides easily into intolerance of dissent. Modern analogues: mission-driven organizations, volunteer-system design, and founder-leads-by-example culture engineering.
modes.source_chapter: 《古巴的社会主义与人》(El socialismo y el hombre en Cuba, 1965)；工业部工作笔记 (1961-1965)；义务劳动制度文件
modes.key_quote_zh: 改造制度的同时必须改造人——否则新人会用旧的方式把新制度重新变回旧制度。
modes.key_quote_en: Remake the system and you must remake the person—otherwise the old man will run the new system back into the old system.
process_zh: 诊断动机结构：盘点当前制度实际依赖的驱动力（薪酬、恐惧、荣誉、意义），识别哪些旧动机正在侵蚀新目标
设计道德激励装置：把志愿服务、荣誉授予、公开表彰做成有频率有仪式感的制度，而非偶尔的口号
领导层先行：领导者必须在最苦的环节以身作则（格瓦拉砍甘蔗、不领薪、拒绝特权），并使之可见可核查
把劳动重构为成长：在组织设计中为成员保留『通过工作改造自己』的通道（学习、创造、跨域挑战），防止劳动纯化为指标游戏
process_en: Diagnose the motive structure: inventory what drives behavior in the current system (pay, fear, honor, meaning) and identify which old motives are corroding the new goals
Design moral-incentive devices: make volunteering, honors, and public recognition into institutions with rhythm and ritual, not occasional slogans
Leaders go first: leaders must set the example in the harshest tasks (Guevara cutting cane, drawing no salary, refusing privilege) and make it visible and verifiable

Reframe work as growth: in organizational design, keep open a channel through which members remake themselves via work (learning, creation, cross-domain challenges), so labor does not reduce to metric games
representative_cases_zh: 义务劳动制度化（1961起）：周六砍甘蔗、港口装货等志愿劳动成为部长与工人同场的固定实践——格瓦拉以此证明道德动员可在国家规模运转，尽管效率争议从未停止
工业部『道德激励vs物质刺激』大辩论（1962-1964）：他主张预算化与精神激励并行，最终古巴采取折中——这场辩论成为二十世纪社会主义经济思想史的重要节点
《古巴的社会主义与人》(1965)在阿尔及尔写就：提出『新人』概念，主张革命者应是一台『由爱驱动的机器』——原文手稿成为后世理想主义者的经典文本
反例警示：纯道德动员在物质极度匮乏期（古巴特别时期）难以为继，且以『不够革命』划线会压制异见——后人需区分『榜样感召』与『道德强制』的边界
representative_cases_en: Institutionalizing voluntary labor (from 1961): Saturday cane-cutting and port loading made ministers and workers co-present in fixed practice—Guevara's proof that moral mobilization can run at national scale, though its efficiency debate never ended

The Ministry of Industries debate, moral vs. material incentives (1962-64): he argued for budgeting alongside spiritual incentives; Cuba settled on a compromise—the debate became a landmark in the history of socialist economic thought

'Socialism and Man in Cuba,' written in Algiers (1965): introduced the 'new man,' declaring the revolutionary should be 'a machine driven by love'—the manuscript became a classic text for later idealists

Counter-case: purely moral mobilization proved hard to sustain through Cuba's Special Period of extreme scarcity, and drawing lines around 'insufficiently revolutionary' suppressed dissent—successors must separate inspirational example from moral coercion
modern_applications_zh: 非营利与开源社区：用署名权、荣誉层级、公开致谢等道德激励替代金钱报酬，维系长期志愿贡献
企业文化：创始人亲自做最难的事并公开可见（一线值班、降薪），比任何价值观海报更能铸造文化
教育与团队：把任务从『完成指标』重构为『通过任务成为什么样的人』，用成长叙事提升内在动机
个人生活：识别自己靠外部奖励运转的领域，为其中最重要的部分重建意义框架，防止内在动机被奖励挤出
modern_applications_en: Nonprofits and open source: sustain long-term volunteer contribution with attribution, honor tiers, and public thanks in place of money
Corporate culture: founders doing the hardest work personally and visibly (frontline shifts, pay cuts) casts culture more strongly than any values poster
Education and teams: reframe tasks from 'hitting metrics' to 'who you become by doing them,' lifting intrinsic motivation through growth narratives
Personal life: identify where you run on external rewards and rebuild a meaning frame for what matters most, guarding against rewards crowding out intrinsic drive

modes.domain_zh: 信念的最终检验不在本国的成功之内而在可输出的实践之中：当一个事业在本国已经完成，就把自身当作可迁移的『方法包』亲自携带到下一处需要的地方，用亲身远征而非道义声援来兑现国际主义
modes.domain_en: The final test of a conviction lies not in domestic success but in exportable practice: once a cause has succeeded at home, carry yourself—as a transferable 'method package'—to the next place that needs it, honoring internationalism through personal expedition rather than moral endorsement
modes.definition_zh: 1965年格瓦拉辞去古巴国籍与一切职务、消失于公众视野，随后出现在刚果，1966年再入玻利维亚——这是二十世纪政治史上罕见的『成功者出走』。方法论内核有三：其一，把成功经验当作可打包的方法而非不可复制的奇迹——他把古巴经验提炼为《游击战》手册，附上地形、组织、医疗、宣传的可操作细节，明确其目的就是让别国的人照着做。其二，『两个、三个、许多个越南』——他在致三大洲人民大会的信中提出：消耗帝国的地方不止一处，远征不是个人英雄主义而是全球战略的分工。其三，亲身性作为最高承诺等级——他判断声援、援助、顾问都不足以证明信念，唯有以自己为耗材的亲自投入才是完全的兑现；『哪里有死亡，我们就欢迎它到来，好让它不能再到别处』。深意在于：他把个人生命当作用来检验并传播方法的最后赌注——方法的可信度最终由创始人愿意为之支付的代价背书。代价是方法不可脱离语境：玻利维亚的失败显示，把一地成功提炼成通用手册时，遗漏的语境变量（农民结构、党派关系、地形）恰恰是决定性的。现代对应物是开源方法论输出、跨国企业出海『亲自落地』与公益组织的在地化投入。
modes.definition_en: In 1965 Guevara renounced his Cuban citizenship and every office, vanished from public view, surfaced in the Congo, and entered Bolivia in 1966—a rare 'exit of the victor' in twentieth-century political history. The method has three cores. First, treat hard-won success as a packagable method, not an unrepeatable miracle: he distilled the Cuban experience into Guerrilla Warfare, with operational detail on terrain, organization, medical care, and propaganda, explicitly so others could follow it. Second, 'two, three, many Vietnams': in his letter to the Tricontinental he argued that the empire must be drained in many places at once—expedition is not personal heroism but a division of labor within a global strategy. Third, physical presence as the highest commitment tier: endorsements, aid, and advice, he judged, cannot prove a conviction; only personal investment with oneself as the consumable fully redeems it—'wherever death may surprise us, let it be welcome, so that it cannot reach anywhere else.' The deeper point: he staked his own life as the final wager for testing and propagating a method—a method's credibility is ultimately underwritten by what its author is willing to pay. The cost: method cannot be severed from context; the Bolivian failure shows that when one locale's success is refined into a universal manual, the omitted contextual variables (peasant structure, party relations, terrain) are precisely the decisive ones. Modern analogues: open-sourcing methodology, founders personally landing foreign expansion, and place-based commitment in aid work.
modes.source_chapter: 《游击战》(1960)；致三大洲人民大会的信 (1967)；刚果笔记 (1965)；玻利维亚日记 (1966-1967)
modes.key_quote_zh: 哪里有死亡，我们就欢迎它到来，好让它不能再到别处去。
modes.key_quote_en: Wherever death may surprise us, let it be welcome, provided that this our war cry may have reached some receptive ear.
process_zh: 提炼方法包：把已验证的经验显性化为可操作的文档（步骤、工具、失败清单），剥离个人色彩使他人可用
选定迁移场域：评估下一个应用地的语境差异（社会结构、在地伙伴、资源禀赋），把『哪些前提必须本地重检』写进方案第一页
配置亲身等级：按承诺强度排序——发声、出资、派员、亲往；识别当前瓶颈在哪一级，把最高级别的资源投向瓶颈
预设退出与失败复盘机制：远征前写明何种信号意味着假设失效，失败后强制完成语境归因（是方法错还是语境错），更新方法包
process_en: Distill the method package: externalize proven experience into operational documents (steps, tools, failure lists), stripping personal color so others can use it

Choose the transfer field: assess contextual differences at the next site of application (social structure, local partners, resource endowments); put 'which premises must be re-verified locally' on page one of the plan
Set the presence tier: rank commitments—speaking, funding, staffing, going in person; identify which tier is the bottleneck and point the highest tier of resource at it

Predefine exit and failure review: state before the expedition which signals would mean the premises have failed; after failure, force a context attribution (wrong method or wrong context) and update the package
representative_cases_zh: 《游击战》(1960)与《游击战：一种手段》(1963)：把古巴经验写成带操作细节的手册公开出版——在方法论上『开源自化』，直接催生了拉美、非洲数十支游击队的诞生与失败
刚果远征 (1965)：应洛朗-卡比拉之邀率古巴顾问团入刚果，因当地指挥体系涣散而撤离，留下《刚果笔记》坦承失败——罕见地把失败原始记录公之于世
玻利维亚远征 (1966-67)：化名『拉蒙』进入，坚持等农民基础而当地党拒绝配合，37岁被俘处决——方法包在语境错配下的终极代价
反例警示：与卡斯特罗的『符合客观条件论』分歧显示，同一方法的创始人内部也存在适用性判断分歧——输出方法时必须携带适用边界，而非只带成功案例
representative_cases_en: Guerrilla Warfare (1960) and Guerrilla Warfare: A Method (1963): publishing the Cuban experience as a manual with operational detail—open-sourcing the method—which directly seeded the birth (and death) of dozens of guerrilla fronts across Latin America and Africa

The Congo expedition (1965): leading a Cuban advisory column at Laurent-Désiré Kabila's invitation, withdrawing amid the local command's disarray, and leaving the Congo Diaries—a rare candid raw record of one's own failure

The Bolivia expedition (1966-67): entering under the alias 'Ramon,' holding out for a peasant base the local party refused to build; captured and executed at 37—the terminal cost of a method package meeting a mismatched context

Counter-case: his split with Castro's 'objective conditions' reading shows even a method's founders disagree on applicability—when exporting a method, ship the applicability boundaries, not just the success story
modern_applications_zh: 开源软件与开源方法论：把内部最佳实践文档化并公开，附带『适用前提』与『已知失败模式』清单
企业出海：方法论输入地必须重做本地验证（渠道、监管、文化），总部经验只作假设不作答案
公益与援助：从『远程资助』升级到『在地驻扎』，把组织的最高承诺等级投向真正的瓶颈
个人职业：把在上一处成功的能力写成可迁移方法，进入新领域时先列『语境差异清单』再动手
modern_applications_en: Open source software and open methodology: publish internal best practices with an 'applicability preconditions' and 'known failure modes' list
Corporate expansion: treat headquarters' experience as hypothesis, never answer; every new market re-runs local validation (channels, regulation, culture)
Aid and philanthropy: upgrade from remote funding to in-place presence, pointing the organization's highest commitment tier at the true bottleneck
Personal careers: write your prior success as a transferable method; on entering a new field, build a context-difference checklist before acting

modes.domain_zh: 把专业技术身份（医生）与政治身份（战士）融合而非分离：技术直接服务于共同体存活，共同体存活的日常目睹反过来供给政治信念——专业与信仰互为对方的事实来源
modes.domain_en: Fuse, rather than separate, a technical identity (physician) with a political one (combatant): technique serves the community's survival directly, and the daily witnessing of that survival feeds conviction back—each identity supplies the other's fact base
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉的人生起点是医生：布宜诺斯艾利斯大学医学系毕业，1952年与阿尔贝托·格拉纳多骑摩托纵贯南美，在秘鲁圣巴勃罗麻风病院做志愿者。医学给了他两样后来决定其革命路径的东西：其一，事实的眼睛——在阿塔卡马矿工、智利铜矿工人、瓜亚基尔病人身上，他看到的不是抽象的『阶级』而是具体的病原：矿肺、营养不良、可治愈却被放弃的病；他在日记里写下『我发现我对人类的判断标准变了』。其二，救治的直觉——起义军中他兼军医，行军时背着药箱、伏击后先救伤员；医疗行为成为游击队获得农民信任的最强纽带，这在foco策略里是战略资产而非个人美德。方法论内核在于：专业技术不是政治事业的装饰，而是它的感官与信用系统——技术身份让政治主张始终锚定在可目睹的具体痛苦上，防止意识形态漂向抽象；政治身份又让技术不被限制为个体善行，而获得结构性的解决方向。代价是角色融合会加剧精神负荷：目睹无法救治的系统性疾病，会驱使人从『治一个人』走向『治一个世界』，超出任何医学的边界。现代对应物是『技术专家+社会倡导』的复合身份（医生参与公共卫生政策、工程师参与气候行动）。
modes.definition_en: Guevara began as a physician: a graduate of Buenos Aires medical school who in 1952 rode a motorcycle across South America with Alberto Granado, volunteering at the San Pablo leprosarium in Peru. Medicine gave him two things that later shaped his revolutionary path. First, the eye for fact: among Atacama miners, Chilean copper workers, and patients in Guayaquil he saw not abstract 'classes' but concrete pathogens—miner's lung, malnutrition, curable diseases abandoned. As he wrote in his diary, 'the measure by which I judge humanity changed.' Second, the reflex of care: in the rebel army he served as combat medic, carrying the kit on the march and treating the wounded first after every ambush; medical care became the guerrillas' strongest bond of peasant trust—a strategic asset within foco strategy, not a personal virtue. The method's core: technical expertise is not decoration for a political cause but its sensory and credit system—the technical identity keeps political claims anchored in observable suffering, preventing ideological drift into abstraction, while the political identity keeps technique from being confined to individual charity and gives it a structural direction. The cost: fused roles compound psychic load—witnessing systemically incurable disease drives one from 'curing a person' to 'curing a world,' beyond any medicine's reach. Modern analogues: hybrid expert-advocate identities (physicians shaping public health policy, engineers in climate action).
modes.source_chapter: 《摩托日记》(Notas de viaje, 1952-53)；马埃斯特腊山军医实践 (1957)；秘鲁圣巴勃罗麻风病院志愿工作
modes.key_quote_zh: 我发现我用来衡量人类的尺子变了——不是从书本上，而是从矿工的肺和病人眼睛里。
modes.key_quote_en: The measure by which I judge humanity changed—not from books, but from the lungs of miners and the eyes of the sick.
process_zh: 用专业去现场：以专业身份进入问题现场（做志愿者、驻场服务），用从业者视角收集一手事实而非二手报告
建立具体档案：把所见系统化为可指认的具体案例与数据（谁的肺、哪个村），作为信念与论证的事实底座
让技术直接服役：在行动组织中承担最能积累信任的技术岗位（医疗、工程、后勤），使专业成为共同体的生命线
双向转译：把个案痛苦转译为结构性议题（从治病人到改制度），同时把宏大目标降维为可执行的技术动作，防止两端失真
process_en: Go to the field with your expertise: enter the problem site under a technical identity (volunteering, resident service) and collect first-hand facts through a practitioner's eyes, not second-hand reports
Build a concrete dossier: systematize what you witness into identifiable cases and data (whose lungs, which village) as the factual bedrock of conviction and argument
Put technique directly in service: in the action organization, hold the technical post that most builds trust (medicine, engineering, logistics), making expertise the community's lifeline

Translate in both directions: convert individual suffering into structural issues (from curing patients to changing systems) while scaling grand goals down into executable technical acts, guarding against distortion at both ends
representative_cases_zh: 1952年摩托之旅：纵贯南美八国，在圣巴勃罗麻风病院为病人游泳训练与护理服务——旅程日记成为后来一切选择的『事实档案』，1953年毕业时已不再是原来的医生
马埃斯特腊山军医格瓦拉：格拉玛号溃败后他背药箱与步枪二选一时两者都带；行医记录成为起义军争取农民支持的核心资产
任国家银行行长与工业部长期间仍以医生自居：他主张经济政策应像临床一样『先诊断后处方』，把工业部治理成一张覆盖全国的『病床统计表』
反例警示：从『治一个人』到『治一个世界』的跃迁没有医学伦理的护栏——他在处决与战争暴力中的决断说明，角色融合若无边界自省会滑向目的证成手段
representative_cases_en: The 1952 motorcycle journey: crossing eight South American countries, serving patients with swimming therapy and care at San Pablo leprosarium—the travel diary became the factual dossier behind every later choice; by graduation in 1953 he was no longer the same doctor

Guevara as combat medic in the Sierra Maestra: after the Granma rout, told to choose between the medical kit and the rifle, he carried both; his medical record became the rebels' core asset in winning peasant support

As bank president and industries minister he still called himself a doctor: he insisted economic policy be clinical—'diagnose before prescribing'—running the ministry like a nationwide chart of beds and symptoms

Counter-case: the leap from 'curing a person' to 'curing a world' has no medical-ethics guardrail; his decisions in executions and war violence show that role fusion without boundary reflection slides into ends justifying means
modern_applications_zh: 专业人的公共参与：医生参与卫生政策、教师参与教育改革、工程师参与气候立法——把技术身份作为公共论证的信用来源
社会企业：创始人保留一线服务岗位的固定时间，防止组织漂离其声称服务的对象
个人职业设计：选择能同时累积『专业纵深』与『现场事实』的位置，让两者互相供养
研究方法：做任何议题先做『田野轮』——以从业者身份亲历，再回到书桌，防止纸上建策略
modern_applications_en: Expert civic participation: physicians shaping health policy, teachers driving school reform, engineers in climate legislation—technical identity as the credit source of public argument
Social enterprise: founders keep fixed hours on the frontline service itself, keeping the organization from drifting from those it claims to serve
Career design: choose positions that build both technical depth and field facts, letting each feed the other
Research method: before any project, run a 'field lap'—experience it as a practitioner before returning to the desk—so strategy is never built on paper

modes.domain_zh: 掌握权力者必须主动清算自己的特权：高官不领额外俸禄、子女不享特殊待遇、亲手放弃已到手的地位与国籍，用对自身的持续剥夺维持与被领导者的道德对等
modes.domain_en: Power-holders must proactively liquidate their own privilege: no extra salary in high office, no special treatment for one's children, personally surrendering attained position and nationality—maintaining moral parity with the led through continuous self-deprivation
modes.definition_zh: 革命胜利后革命者去哪里？格瓦拉给出的答案是：去清算自己。他在古巴先后任国家银行行长（1959）与工业部长（1961-1965），是政权经济实际掌舵人之一，但他的自律清单近乎苛刻：任部长期间拒绝涨薪，全家按原有标准生活；孩子不许进特殊学校、不许有特权物品；1959年访日时拒绝下榻豪华酒店；1965年干脆辞去一切职务、放弃古巴国籍，消失在刚果丛林。方法有三：其一，把特权视为敌方的武器——他判断革命政权最大的腐蚀不是外部封锁而是干部层与群众生活水平的拉开，特权每一寸都在给对手提供宣传弹药。其二，『道德对等』原则——领导者若要求群众承担义务，必须以自己先承担更重的义务为前提，这是他义务劳动制度的个人版本。其三，用退出为信念定价——他相信领导人最大的考验是能否走出自己的成功，1965年的出走把『能上能下』做到了极致。深意在于：他把权力自律从『不做坏事』升级为『主动消除做坏事的资本』，以身位差为零作为组织合法性的基准线。代价是：以个人操守替代制度约束不可复制也不可审计。现代对应物是创始人的薪酬公开、高管问责文化与『以身入局』式自律。
modes.definition_en: Where does a revolutionary go after victory? Guevara's answer: to liquidate oneself. President of the National Bank (1959) then Minister of Industries (1961-65), a de facto helmsman of the economy, he kept a nearly severe self-audit list: as minister he refused raises, keeping his family at its previous standard; his children were barred from special schools and privilege items; visiting Japan in 1959 he declined a luxury hotel; and in 1965 he simply resigned every post, renounced his Cuban citizenship, left his parents a farewell letter signing 'your stray horse,' and vanished into the Congo. The method has three parts. First, treat privilege as the enemy's weapon: the greatest corrosion of a revolutionary regime, he judged, is not external blockade but the widening gap between cadres and the masses—every inch of privilege hands the adversary propaganda ammunition. Second, the principle of moral parity: if leaders demand obligations from the people, they must first bear heavier obligations themselves—his personal version of the voluntary-labor system. Third, price conviction with exit: the greatest test of a leader, he believed, is walking out of one's own success; the 1965 departure pushed 'able to rise, able to step down' to its limit. The deeper point: he upgraded power self-discipline from 'not doing wrong' to 'actively eliminating the capital for doing wrong,' setting zero status differential as the baseline of organizational legitimacy. The cost: substituting personal conduct for institutional constraint is neither replicable nor auditable, and it exerts moral pressure on peers that cannot be sustained. Modern analogues: founder salary transparency, executive accountability rituals, and leader-steps-into-the-arena audit culture.
modes.source_chapter: 致父母的告别信 (1965)；古巴政府任职记录 (1959-1965)；义务劳动实践与拒绝涨薪记录
key_concepts: 以身位差为零定合法性
modes.key_quote_zh: 革命者真正的考验，不是能否夺取政权，而是能否走出自己已经握在手中的政权。
modes.key_quote_en: The true revolutionary's test is not seizing power but walking out of the power already in hand.
process_zh: 盘点特权资产：列出职位带来的全部隐性收益（薪酬外待遇、家人便利、信息优势、名义资本），形成自我清算清单
公开化与可核查：把自律标准公之于众并设置可核查的形式（工资条、公开日程、家属待遇），让『以身作则』不靠传闻
以更重义务对冲权力：每次行使权力都配套一次更重的自我承担（更苦的岗位、更长的劳动、更少的报酬）
预设退出条款：在心理与制度上预留『功成身退』的路径——主动放弃比被迫失去更能为信念定价
process_en: Inventory privilege assets: list every implicit gain office brings (perks, family convenience, information advantage, nominal capital) into a self-liquidation register
Make it public and verifiable: publish one's self-discipline standards in checkable form (pay slips, open schedules, family treatment), so leading by example rests on records, not rumor
Offset power with heavier duty: pair every exercise of power with a heavier self-burden (harsher post, longer labor, smaller pay)
Predefine an exit clause: reserve, psychologically and institutionally, a path of stepping down at the summit—voluntary surrender prices conviction far better than forced loss
representative_cases_zh: 拒涨薪与家庭标准冻结：任工业部长期间坚持与普通公务员同等工资，家庭生活标准不随职位上移——以可核查的工资单而非道德口号自律
子女不许特权：孩子的学校与用品一律按普通标准，拒绝利用职位为其铺路——把『反腐』从办公桌延伸到饭桌
1965年出走：辞去部长、放弃古巴国籍、告别信署名『你的野马』——在声望顶点主动清零，成为二十世纪政治人物自我放逐的极端样本
反例警示：他的清算法依赖个人极高标准且无制度保障，同侪未必可复制；以圣人标准要求他人易造成组织内部的道德窒息——现代组织中必须把个人自律转化为制度设计
representative_cases_en: Refusing raises, freezing the family standard: as industries minister he took a civil-service-equal salary and kept household standards flat—self-audit via checkable pay slips, not moral slogans
No privilege for his children: schools and belongings all at ordinary standards, never using office to pave their way—extending 'anti-corruption' from the desk to the dinner table

The 1965 departure: resigning the ministry, renouncing Cuban citizenship, the farewell letter signed 'your stray horse'—voluntary zeroing at the peak of prestige, an extreme case of political self-exile in the twentieth century

Counter-case: his method relied on one man's extreme standards with no institutional guarantee, and peers could not necessarily copy it; demanding sainthood of others breeds moral suffocation—modern organizations must convert personal discipline into institutional design
modern_applications_zh: 创始人与高管：公开薪酬与相关方利益清单，任内冻结个人待遇增长，把『公司利益与个人利益分离』做成可审计事实
公共机构：官员亲属利益申报制度化，杜绝以岗位为家人铺路的灰色通道
项目管理：负责人在资源分配时给自己配最少的份额与最重的交付，以身位差为零维系团队信任
个人成长：在获得声望的每个节点预设『退出条款』——事先写下何时、以何种方式让出位置
modern_applications_en: Founders and executives: publish pay and interest registers, freeze personal treatment growth in office, make 'corporate interest apart from private interest' an auditable fact
Public institutions: institutionalize disclosure of officials' relatives' interests, closing gray channels of paving family paths with office
Project management: when allocating resources, the lead takes the smallest share and heaviest deliverable—zero status differential as the trust base of a team
Personal growth: at every prestige milestone, pre-write an exit clause—when, and in what manner, you will give up the seat

modes.domain_zh: 弱者不打消耗战而打杠杆战：把敌人的优势（装备、兵力、声望）设计成自己的放大器——迫其分散、迫其镇压、迫其升级，让对手的每一次优势发挥都转化为己方的动员资源
modes.domain_en: The weak do not fight wars of attrition but wars of leverage: design the enemy's strengths—equipment, numbers, prestige—as your own amplifier—forcing him to disperse, to repress, to escalate—so every exercise of his advantage converts into your mobilization resource
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉的军事写作反复回到一个不等式：政府军必须处处设防，游击队只需选择一处进攻；敌人维持全国秩序每天要花巨量成本，游击队的每一天只需要活下来。方法有三：其一，迫使分散——游击队的存在本身迫使政府军把兵力撒向山区与农村，稀释其在城市的控制力；马埃斯特腊山的一百人牵制了数万政府军。其二，镇压即动员——敌人的过度反应（轰炸村庄、连坐、处决）被预制为宣传资产：每一次暴行都在为起义军招募新的志愿者；他明确要求游击队纪律严明、不扰民、优待俘虏，就是为了把『镇压的镜子』打磨得更亮。其三，升级即暴露——当敌人被迫动用外国援助或极端手段（如巴蒂斯塔的空中轰炸），其政权失去合法性的进程被加速；格瓦拉甚至把美国的介入视为战略收益。深意在于：他重新定义了『损失』——只要能把对手拖入花费巨大而收益为零的行动，己方就算每天都在撤退也是每天都在得分。代价是这套杠杆要求极强的纪律与信息控制：一旦己方暴行对等出现，杠杆立即反转。现代对应物是商业中以小博大的不对称竞争、舆论战中的『过度反应陷阱』与安全领域的防御经济学。
modes.definition_en: Guevara's military writing returns to one inequality: a government army must defend everywhere, while guerrillas attack where they choose; the enemy pays enormous daily costs to hold national order, while the guerrilla's daily cost is only survival. The method has three parts. First, force dispersion: the mere existence of the foco forces the army to scatter into mountains and countryside, diluting urban control—a hundred men in the Sierra Maestra pinned down tens of thousands. Second, repression is mobilization: the enemy's overreactions (bombing villages, collective punishment, executions) are pre-designed as propaganda assets—each atrocity recruits new volunteers; his strict discipline, no harassment of civilians, and good treatment of prisoners existed precisely to polish that mirror of repression. Third, escalation is exposure: when the enemy resorts to foreign aid or extreme means (Batista's aerial bombing), the regime loses legitimacy faster; Guevara even counted American intervention as a strategic gain. The deeper point: he redefined 'loss'—so long as the opponent is dragged into high-cost, zero-yield operations, the weak side scores every day it retreats. The cost: this leverage demands extreme discipline and information control; the instant equivalent atrocities appear on one's own side, the lever reverses. Modern analogues: asymmetric competition of small against large, the 'overreaction trap' in public opinion warfare, and defense economics in security.
modes.source_chapter: 《游击战》(1960)第二章『游击队的战略』；圣克拉拉战役与列车伏击战记录；《致三大洲的信》
modes.key_quote_zh: 让敌人每一发炮弹都为我们的队伍招募新兵——他打得越狠，我们的人越多。
modes.key_quote_en: Let every enemy shell recruit new soldiers for our columns—the harder he strikes, the more we grow.
process_zh: 画出成本不对称：对比敌我维持同一空间的每日成本（兵力、补给、政治代价），选择己方成本趋近于零、对手成本极高的博弈点
制造过度反应：以低代价行动（伏击、破袭、宣传）诱使对手动用不成比例的力量，并将每一次过度反应即时转化为宣传与招募素材
纪律即战略资产：把善待平民、优待俘虏、不扰民写成硬性军纪，因为己方的克制是对手暴行的对比放大器
诱使升级并收割暴露：诱导对手引入外部势力或极端手段，让其在国际与国内舆论中暴露，加速其合法性流失
process_en: Draw the cost asymmetry: compare the enemy's and your daily costs of holding the same space (troops, supply, political price); pick博弈 points where your cost approaches zero and his is extreme
Provoke overreaction: use low-cost actions (ambush, sabotage, propaganda) to lure disproportionate force, converting each overreaction in real time into propaganda and recruitment material
Discipline as strategic asset: write kindness to civilians, good treatment of prisoners, and non-harassment into hard military law—your restraint is the contrast amplifier of his brutality
Lure escalation and harvest exposure: induce the opponent to bring in outside forces or extreme measures, exposing him before domestic and international opinion and accelerating his legitimacy loss
representative_cases_zh: 马埃斯特腊山牵制战：数百人起义军把数万政府军拖进山区消耗，巴蒂斯塔的空袭炸毁村庄反而让农民成批上山——镇压即动员的经典演示
优待俘虏政策：起义军俘虏政府军士兵后发路费遣散，甚至就地吸收参军——把敌军士气系统性瓦解，1958年政府军逃兵潮证明了这一点
圣克拉拉装甲列车伏击 (1958)：用简单器材瘫痪一列装甲列车、俘获数百人与大量装备——一次战斗同时完成缴械与心理瓦解，数日后哈瓦那易手
反例警示：拉美多国游击队模仿此法却忽视纪律前提，绑架、爆炸伤及平民后杠杆立即反转，民心思定——杠杆战对己方纪律的要求不比对武器的要求低
representative_cases_en: The Sierra Maestra pinning battle: a few hundred rebels dragged tens of thousands of government troops into mountain attrition; Batista's air raids on villages drove peasants up the mountain in batches—repression as mobilization demonstrated
The good-treatment prisoner policy: captured soldiers were paid and released, or absorbed on the spot—systematically dissolving enemy morale; the 1958 wave of army desertions proved it

The Santa Clara armored-train ambush (1958): simple tools derailed an armored train, capturing hundreds of men and a mass of equipment—one battle completing both disarmament and psychological collapse; Havana changed hands days later

Counter-case: Latin American imitators copied the method while ignoring its disciplinary premise; kidnappings and bombings hitting civilians reversed the lever instantly and turned publics toward order—leverage war demands as much of your discipline as of your weapons
modern_applications_zh: 不对称商业竞争：小公司不打全面战争，只在大对手『必须防 everywhere』的成本结构里选点突破（细分场景、合规盲区、服务体验）
舆情与公关：设计让对手『过度回应』的低成本动作，把对方的压制性声明变成己方的传播素材
安全与风控：把防御预算投向『迫使攻击者成本上升』的环节，以防御经济学而非堆砌设备取胜
个人谈判：面对强势方，不比拼资源而比拼耐心与成本曲线，把对方的每次施压转化为己方的正当性证明
modern_applications_en: Asymmetric business competition: the small firm avoids total war and strikes where the incumbent 'must defend everywhere' at cost—niche scenarios, compliance blind spots, service experience
PR and opinion warfare: design low-cost moves that provoke overreaction, turning the adversary's repressive statements into your own amplification material
Security and risk: aim defense budgets at forcing attacker costs up—winning by defense economics rather than equipment stacking
Personal negotiation: against a stronger party, compete on patience and the cost curve, not resources—converting every act of pressure into proof of your legitimacy

modes.domain_zh: 以不间断的现场日记作为自我审计与信念校准工具：每天记录事实、情绪与自我批评，既给行动留下可复盘的原始档案，又迫使理想主义者定期直面自己的幻觉与失误
modes.domain_en: Use uninterrupted field diaries as instruments of self-audit and conviction calibration: record facts, emotions, and self-criticism daily—leaving a raw archive for after-action review while forcing the idealist to face his own illusions and errors on a schedule
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉从1952年的摩托之旅到1967年玻利维亚的最后一夜，保持了整整十五年几乎不间断的日记写作，多数在丛林、行军与炮火间隙完成。方法论上有三重功能：其一，事实底账——日记是他一切写作（《游击战》《革命战争随笔》）的原材料，现场的日期、地名、伤亡、补给都被即时固定，避免事后的记忆美化；他在《游击战》里的许多论断都能回溯到具体某夜的记录。其二，自我批评装置——刚果笔记里他直书当地盟友的涣散，也写自己的误判与部队的混乱，把失败当作数据而非耻辱；玻利维亚日记里他逐月记录『招募无进展』『哮喘恶化』『与党谈判破裂』，直到最后一天仍在记录。其三，信念的化验单——日记让他能在理想与现实之间定期做『指标对比』：当现实持续偏离理想而他仍选择前进时，这是经过计算的固执而非一时冲动。深意在于：他把自我怀疑制度化——不是靠毅力维持信念，而是靠一份持续更新的证据文件让信念接受检验。代价是：日记的诚实被公开后可能成为对手的武器（他的日记在他死后由古巴整理出版，也成为研究者批评foco论的原始证据）。现代对应物是决策日志、复盘文化与实验记录本。
modes.definition_en: From the 1952 motorcycle journey to his last night in Bolivia in 1967, Guevara kept diaries nearly without interruption for fifteen years, most written in jungle camps, on the march, in the gaps between bombardments. Methodologically it served three functions. First, the factual ledger: the diaries were the raw material of all his writing (Guerrilla Warfare, Episodes of the Revolutionary War); dates, places, casualties, and supply were fixed in real time, forestalling hindsight beautification—many claims in Guerrilla Warfare trace back to a specific night's entry. Second, a device of self-criticism: in the Congo Diaries he wrote plainly of his allies' disarray and of his own misjudgments and the column's chaos, treating failure as data, not shame; in the Bolivia Diary he logged month by month 'no recruitment progress,' 'asthma worsening,' 'talks with the party broken'—recording to the final day. Third, a lab report on conviction: the diaries let him run periodic comparisons between ideal and reality; when reality kept diverging and he still chose to advance, that was calculated obstinacy, not impulse. The deeper point: he institutionalized self-doubt—conviction sustained not by willpower but by a continuously updated evidence file that belief itself must pass. The cost: diaries, once public, arm the adversary; published posthumously by Cuba, they also became the primary evidence on which critics convicted foco theory. Modern analogues: decision logs, after-action review culture, lab notebooks.
modes.source_chapter: 《玻利维亚日记》(Diario de Bolivia, 1966-67)；《刚果笔记》(Pasajes de la guerra revolucionaria: Congo, 1965)；《摩托日记》(1952-53)
modes.key_quote_zh: 把每天发生的事原样写下来——不是为了记住自己多正确，而是为了看清自己错在哪里。
modes.key_quote_en: Write each day as it happened—not to remember how right you were, but to see clearly where you went wrong.
process_zh: 固定格式每日记录：日期、事实、情绪、自我批评四栏缺一不可，尤其在最艰苦、最不想写的日子强制执行
区分事实与解释：先原样记录发生了什么，再写判断，两层分开——防止记忆随立场改写
定期对照检查：每月把日记中的预期与现实结果并排复盘，识别系统性偏差并调整下一步假设
失败强制归档：重大失败必须写完整复盘（发生了什么、我误判了什么、下次改变什么），可公开的公开，让失败成为组织资产
process_en: Fixed-format daily entries: date, facts, emotion, self-criticism—four columns, none optional, enforced especially on the hardest days when writing is least wanted
Separate fact from interpretation: record what happened verbatim first, then the judgment, in two distinct layers—keeping memory from being rewritten by stance
Periodic comparison checks: each month, review expectations against outcomes side by side, identify systematic bias, and adjust the next set of assumptions

Mandatory failure archiving: every major failure gets a complete postmortem (what happened, what I misjudged, what changes next time); publish what can be published, making failure an organizational asset
representative_cases_zh: 《摩托日记》(1952)：八个月的旅程逐日成文，青年格瓦拉的自我认知转变有完整轨迹可查——这份日记成为他日后一切选择的原始档案
《革命战争随笔》：大量段落直接取自古巴战争时期的战地日记，日期与细节可核对——写作因此具有档案级可信度
《刚果笔记》坦承撤离：直书『这是一场失败』并分析原因，死后出版——罕见地把领导人自己的失败复盘作为公开教材
《玻利维亚日记》：直到被俘前一日仍在记录体力、士气与判断的恶化；后世研究者正是依据这份诚实记录重构了foco论失效的完整链条
representative_cases_en: The Motorcycle Diaries (1952): eight months rendered day by day, giving the young Guevara's transformation a fully traceable arc—the diary became the raw archive behind every later choice
Episodes of the Revolutionary War: many passages lifted straight from wartime field diaries, dates and details cross-checkable—writing with archival-grade credibility
The Congo Diaries confessing withdrawal: plainly stating 'this was a failure' and analyzing why, published posthumously—a leader's own failure postmortem offered openly as a teaching text

The Bolivia Diary: recording his physical decline, morale, and judgment until the day before capture; researchers later reconstructed the full chain of foco theory's failure precisely from this honest record
modern_applications_zh: 决策日志：重要决策当场记录『当时知道什么、为何这么选』，半年后复盘，防止结果论改写记忆
团队复盘文化：项目结束强制写『我们错在哪』的备忘并归档共享，把失败转化为组织的学习资产
实验记录本：科研与产品开发中区分『观察』与『假设』两栏，保证结论可回溯
个人成长：每晚四栏日记（事实/情绪/自我批评/明日调整），用十年尺度积累一份对自己的诚实档案
modern_applications_en: Decision logs: record at decision time 'what we knew and why we chose this,' review six months later—keeping outcome bias from rewriting memory
Team postmortem culture: end every project with a mandatory 'where we were wrong' memo, archived and shared, turning failure into organizational learning assets
Lab notebooks: in research and product development, keep observation and hypothesis in separate columns so conclusions stay traceable
Personal growth: a nightly four-column diary (facts / emotion / self-criticism / tomorrow's adjustment), accumulating ten years of an honest file on yourself

modes.domain_zh: 在生命终点把形象本身当作最后一项工作来经营：选择极具视觉张力的死亡叙事（被俘照片、殉难现场、公开遗容），让肉体的失败转化为符号的永生——死后影响力反超生前
modes.domain_en: Treat one's own image as the final work at life's end: choose a death narrative of extreme visual force (the captured photograph, the martyrdom scene, the publicly displayed corpse) so that bodily defeat converts into symbolic immortality—influence after death outrunning influence in life
modes.definition_zh: 1967年10月9日，玻利维亚军方处决格瓦拉后，指示冲洗他遗体的照片并向媒体展示，本意是证明『切已死』以瓦解游击运动。结果成为二十世纪传播学的经典反噬案例：遗体照片与耶稣受难像的视觉同构瞬间点燃全球，几个月内他的形象横扫欧洲学生运动与第三世界解放阵线；1960年科达在哈瓦那葬礼上拍摄的《英勇的游击队员》后来成为史上复制量最大的照片之一。方法论内核有三：其一，视觉预埋——他生前就高度自觉形象的力量：摄影、电影、演说的姿态都有经营痕迹；蓄须、军装、贝雷帽上的红星，构成一套极易复制传播的极简符号系统。其二，殉难叙事的结构——他在最后的信里写『我的死将比我的生更有用』，把死亡本身设计为一次传播事件：被俘时不求饶、受审时直言、遗容公开展示，每一个环节都在为符号增值。其三，死后去个人化——符号一旦脱离版权（古巴有意不主张肖像版权），便以病毒方式扩散；『切』成为全球通用的一种『纯洁反抗』的能指。深意在于：他证明了影响力的最后一环不在生前的成就而在死后叙事的可复制性。代价是符号化即失真——被消费的『切』与其历史中的暴力与复杂性几乎脱钩。现代对应物是个人品牌遗产设计、开源视觉识别系统与meme传播工程。
modes.definition_en: On October 9, 1967, after executing Guevara, the Bolivian military ordered photographs of his corpse taken and shown to the press, intending to prove 'Che is dead' and break the guerrilla movement. It became a classic case of backfire in twentieth-century communication: the visual isomorphism of the corpse with the Passion of Christ ignited the globe within months—his image swept the European student movements, Third World liberation fronts, and the antiwar wave; Alberto Korda's 1960 'Guerrillero Heroico,' taken at a Havana funeral, became one of the most reproduced photographs in history, printed on everything from T-shirts to cigar boxes. The method has three cores. First, visual pre-planting: he was acutely conscious of image power in life—beard, fatigues, cigar, the red star on the beret composed a minimal symbol system built for replication. Second, the structure of martyrdom: in his final letters he wrote that his death would be more useful than his life, designing death itself as a communication event—no begging when captured, plain speech at interrogation, the corpse displayed—each step adding value to the symbol. Third, de-propertization after death: once the symbol left copyright (Cuba deliberately declined to enforce portrait rights), it spread virally; 'Che' became a universal signifier of 'pure resistance,' though most users know little of the history. The deeper point: the last link of influence lies not in lifetime achievement but in the replicability of the posthumous narrative. The cost: symbolization is distortion—the consumed 'Che' is decoupled from the violence and complexity of the historical record; symbolic immortality is purchased with historical blur. Modern analogues: personal brand legacy design, open-source visual identity, and meme engineering.
modes.source_chapter: 1967年10月遗体照片事件；科达《英勇的游击队员》(1960)；《致儿女的信》与告别信；遗容公开展示记录
modes.key_quote_zh: 我的死将比我的生更有用。
modes.key_quote_en: My death will be more useful than my life.
process_zh: 构建极简符号集：提炼可被一行文字描述的视觉元素（形象、服饰、标志性姿态），确保低成本可复制
预写终章叙事：提前设计生命/事业终点的呈现方式与文本（告别信、最后声明），让结局本身成为传播事件而非意外
选择可传播的失败形态：即便失败也要让失败叙事具备尊严、张力与道德高位，避免仓皇与混乱主导最后画面
释放符号版权：放弃对形象的商业与话语垄断，允许其被再创作与误用，以扩散性换取生命力的延长
process_en: Build a minimal symbol set: distill visual elements describable in one line (image, dress, signature gesture), ensuring low-cost replicability
Pre-write the final chapter: design in advance how the end—of life or of the cause—will be presented (farewell letter, last statement), making the ending a communication event, not an accident
Choose a transmissible form of defeat: even in failure, give the narrative dignity, tension, and the moral high ground—never let panic and chaos own the final frame
Release the symbol's copyright: renounce commercial and discursive monopoly on the image, permitting reuse and even misuse—buying longevity with diffusiveness
representative_cases_zh: 遗体照片反噬 (1967)：军方展示遗容本为终结神话，照片的『受难像』视觉结构反而在全球制造殉道者——传播史上意图与效果错位的标志性案例
科达《英勇的游击队员》(1960)：哈瓦那葬礼上一次偶然的仰角抓拍，因构图简洁成为全球复制量最大的照片之一——极简符号的可复制性实证
古巴不主张肖像版权：『切』形象被自由用于商品、艺术与抗议，符号以病毒速度扩散——去个人化的传播工程使影响力远超其政治组织所能覆盖
反例警示：符号成功与历史真实脱钩——被印上商品的『切』遮蔽了他在古巴革命初期的处决行为与经济治理争议；经营符号者须接受符号脱离自己意志的命运
representative_cases_en: The corpse-photo backfire (1967): the army's display meant to kill the myth instead manufactured a global martyr—the Passion-like visual structure doing the work—the landmark case of intent and effect diverging in communication history

Korda's 'Guerrillero Heroico' (1960): a casual low-angle shot at a Havana funeral, its spare composition becoming one of history's most reproduced photographs—empirical proof of minimal-symbol replicability

Cuba declining to enforce portrait rights: the Che image freed for commerce, art, and protest, spreading at viral speed—a de-propertied communication project whose reach far exceeded any political organization

Counter-case: symbolic success decoupled from historical truth—the Che on merchandise obscures his role in early-revolution executions and contested economic governance; whoever cultivates a symbol must accept its life beyond his own will
modern_applications_zh: 个人品牌终局设计：提前规划你希望被记住的一张照片、一句话、一个姿态，并确保其视觉极简可复制
开源视觉识别：公益与技术项目主动开放logo与视觉资产的使用，以传播力置换控制力
纪念性叙事：创始人/领导者的离任与谢幕应作为精心设计的传播事件，而非被动安排
警惕符号失真：接受符号被简化消费的同时，预置可查证的历史档案入口（自传、档案、公开日记）供深度使用者回溯
modern_applications_en: Personal-brand endgame design: plan in advance the one photo, one sentence, one gesture you wish to be remembered by—and keep it visually minimal and replicable
Open-source visual identity: civic and technical projects open logo and visual assets for use, trading control for reach
Commemorative narrative: a founder's or leader's departure and curtain call should be a designed communication event, not a passive arrangement
Guard against symbol distortion: accept simplification while pre-installing a verifiable archive entry (memoir, records, published diaries) for users who go deeper

modes.domain_zh: 把长途旅行本身做成认知装置：不靠文献与统计理解一个大陆，而以身体移动穿过其地形、疾病、阶层与日常，让地理经验直接重塑认知框架
modes.domain_en: Make the long journey itself a cognitive instrument: not understanding a continent through literature and statistics but traversing its terrain, disease, class, and daily life with one's body in motion, letting geographic experience directly reshape the cognitive frame
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉的两次长途旅行（1952年摩托纵贯南美、1953-56年穿越中美洲到墨西哥）是方法论意义上的『认知重构实验』：他后来明确说，是路上的所见而非书上的理论使他成为革命者。方法有三：其一，低防护穿行——他选择搭便车、做搬运工、睡码头的方式移动，主动放弃游客的安全层，使身体直接暴露于所经社会的真实运行（智利铜矿的粉尘、秘鲁麻风病院的病房、巴拿马的贫困街区），感知通道全开。其二，工作即接口——每到一处以行医、做工换取进入当地人生活的资格，医生身份让他被允许看见家庭内部的健康与贫困，这是任何采访者拿不到的入口。其三，边走边写——每天把见闻写进日记并邮寄，把流动经验即时固化为文本；后来他称这次旅行让『我离开时是一个人，回来时是另一个人』。深意在于：地理尺度本身就是一种知识论——统计数字告诉你『有多少人穷』，穿过它们的身体告诉你『穷是什么感觉、以何种结构存在』；前者供论证，后者供动机。代价是：旅程式认知样本有限且高度依赖个体遭遇，容易从个案过度推广为大陆级结论。现代对应物是沉浸式田野调查、间隔年式职业转换与『深入一线』的产品调研。
modes.definition_en: Guevara's two long journeys (the 1952 motorcycle circuit of South America, and 1953-56 through Central America to Mexico) were cognitive-reconstruction experiments in the methodological sense: he later said plainly that what he saw on the road, not theory in books, made him a revolutionary. The method has three parts. First, low-shield travel: hitchhiking, working as a mover, sleeping on docks—deliberately shedding the tourist's safety layer so the body is directly exposed to the real operation of the societies passed through (dust in Chilean copper mines, wards in the Peruvian leprosarium, poor districts of Panama), all perception channels open. Second, work as interface: arriving everywhere, he traded medicine and labor for the right to enter local life; the doctor's identity let him see inside households—health and poverty together—an entry no interviewer gets. Third, writing in motion: daily entries mailed home fixed flowing experience into text; he later said he 'left as one person and returned as another.' The deeper point: geographic scale is itself an epistemology—statistics tell you how many are poor; a body moving through them tells you what poverty feels like and how it is structured. The former feeds argument, the latter motive. The cost: journey-based cognition has a small sample and depends heavily on individual encounters, easily over-generalizing from cases to continent-scale conclusions. Modern analogues: immersive fieldwork, career-gap immersion, and 'go to the frontline' product research.
modes.source_chapter: 《摩托日记》(1952-53)；1953-56年拉美穿越行程；《革命战争随笔》自述
modes.key_quote_zh: 我离开时是一个人，回来时是另一个人——改变我的不是书本，是路上的尘土与病房。
modes.key_quote_en: I left as one person and returned as another—what changed me was not books but the dust and the wards along the road.
process_zh: 设计低防护路线：选择放弃便利与安全的行进方式（公共交通、体力工作、当地食宿），把自己暴露在目标社会的真实运行中
以技能换入口：用自己可提供的专业（医疗、技术、教学）换取进入当地人生活的资格，采集从外部拿不到的一手信息
移动中即时记录：每天固定输出文字或影像并归档，把流动经验在记忆美化前固化
旅程结束做认知对账：列出『哪些看法被推翻、哪些新框架形成』，并标注哪些结论只是个案推广，防止样本偏差变成世界观
process_en: Design a low-shield route: pick modes of travel that forfeit comfort and safety (public transport, manual work, local food and lodging), exposing yourself to the target society's real operation
Trade skill for entry: exchange what you can offer (medicine, technical help, teaching) for the right to enter local life, gathering first-hand information unavailable from outside
Record in motion: fixed daily output of text or image, archived, fixing flowing experience before memory beautifies it

Cognitive reconciliation at journey's end: list 'which views were overturned, which new frames formed,' and flag which conclusions are case-level generalizations—keeping sample bias from hardening into worldview
representative_cases_zh: 1952年摩托之旅：从布宜诺斯艾利斯到迈阿密的八个月穿越，智利矿工、秘鲁麻风病人、哥伦比亚内战沿途所见构成他对『拉丁美洲是一个整体』认知的经验底座
圣巴勃罗麻风病院之夜：他与同伴为病人举办生日会、陪病人游泳，越过职业距离——这一夜他在日记里写下对『边界』与『共同体』的重新理解
1953-56年的第二次旅行：经玻利维亚、秘鲁、中美到墨西哥，途中目睹阿本兹政权被政变推翻——『帝国主义如何运作』从理论变成亲眼所见的剧本，直接推动他转向武装斗争
反例警示：旅程认知让他对拉美形成高度个人化的判断，foco论的过度推广部分源于把个人旅程样本误当作大陆规律——旅行者需警惕把最震撼的遭遇当作最普遍的规律
representative_cases_en: The 1952 motorcycle journey: eight months from Buenos Aires toward Miami; Chilean miners, Peruvian leprosy patients, and Colombia's civil war along the way formed the experiential bedrock of his conviction that 'Latin America is one'

The night at San Pablo leprosarium: he and his companion threw a birthday party for patients and swam with them across the professional distance—the night he rewrote, in the diary, his sense of 'borders' and 'community'

The second journey, 1953-56: via Bolivia, Peru, and Central America to Mexico, witnessing the coup that toppled Árbenz—'how imperialism works' turned from theory into a script he had watched being performed, pushing him toward armed struggle

Counter-case: journey cognition bred a highly personal judgment of Latin America; foco theory's overreach partly stems from mistaking one traveler's sample for a continental law—the traveler must beware taking the most striking encounter for the most general rule
modern_applications_zh: 产品调研：做全球市场前先以普通用户身份在目标地区生活数周（用当地收入、坐当地通勤），样本虽小但直击结构性现实
教育与成长：把间隔年设计为『低防护+技能置换』结构，而非消费式观光
管理与领导：新任高管先做一轮一线轮岗（客服、车间、配送），用身体经验替代报表认知
写作与研究：长途田野后先做『认知对账』再立论，标注个案与规律的边界
modern_applications_en: Product research: before entering a new market, live in the target region for weeks as an ordinary user (local income, local commute)—a small sample that hits structural reality directly
Education and growth: structure a gap year as 'low-shield travel plus skill exchange,' not consumption tourism
Management and leadership: a new executive starts with frontline rotations (support, shop floor, delivery), replacing report cognition with bodily experience
Writing and research: after long fieldwork, run the cognitive reconciliation before arguing—marking the border between case and law

modes.domain_zh: 在事业的关键岔口，用终局视角而非当下得失做选择：当理想与既得利益、个人安危、组织路线冲突时，以『哪条路让理想在十年尺度上仍活着』为唯一裁决标准，并为此支付当下代价
modes.domain_en: At the critical forks of a cause, choose by the endgame view rather than present gains: when the ideal conflicts with vested interest, personal safety, or the organizational line, take as sole arbiter the question 'which path keeps the ideal alive on a ten-year scale,' and pay today's price for it
modes.definition_zh: 格瓦拉一生的重大转折都可由一条原则解释：理想优先于舒适、优先于职位、优先于安全，甚至优先于自己的生命。1965年他离开的是自己亲手参与缔造、正处于上升期的政权与个人声望的顶点；1966年他进入的是成功率近乎为零的玻利维亚丛林。他不是不知道风险——玻利维亚日记逐日记录了他对困境的清醒评估——他是在知情之后仍然选择。方法论内核有三：其一，终局标准前置——在每一次岔口用『十年后什么还重要』过滤选项，把当下收益（官位、安全、关系）降权，把理想的存活率升权；他给卡斯特罗的告别信、给子女的信都以此语气写成。其二，为选择支付全额代价——他拒绝半吊子方案，而选择把姓名、职位、国籍、生命全部押上，因为他判断半额投入会让理想在执行中变形。其三，知情之下的固执——日记显示他清楚每一步的成功率在下降，但他的判断框架是『只要火种存在一天，起义的可能性就存在一天』。深意在于：他示范了一种罕见的选择算法——不是最大化成功的概率，而是最大化理想在历史中存活的概率。代价是：这种算法对执行者与追随者的消耗都极大，且在组织层面不可推广为常规制度。现代对应物是创始人『为使命放弃退出机会』的抉择与个人生涯中的价值排序决策。
modes.definition_en: Every major turn of Guevara's life is explained by a single principle: the ideal outranks comfort, outranks office, outranks safety—even outranks his own life. What he left in 1965 was a rising regime he had helped build and the peak of personal prestige; what he entered in 1966 was the Bolivian jungle, with success odds near zero. He was not blind to the risk—the Bolivia Diary logs his clear-eyed assessment of the worsening situation daily—he chose after knowing. The method has three cores. First, the endgame criterion up front: at every fork, filter options through 'what will still matter in ten years,' downweighting present yield (office, safety, connections) and upweighting the ideal's survival odds; his farewell letter to Castro and letters to his children are written in exactly that register. Second, paying the full price of the choice: he refused half measures (a sinecure in a third country as 'endorser') and staked name, office, nationality, and life together, judging that half-investment deforms the ideal in execution. Third, obstinacy under knowledge: the diary shows he knew each step lowered the odds, yet his frame was 'so long as the spark exists one day, the possibility of insurrection exists one day'—handing the verdict from probability to value. The deeper point: he demonstrated a rare choice algorithm—not maximizing the probability of success but maximizing the probability that the ideal survives in history, even with oneself as the only carrier. The cost: the algorithm consumes executors and followers alike and cannot be generalized into routine institutions. Modern analogues: founders forgoing exits for the mission, scientists' long bets on the true problems, and value-ranking decisions in a personal career.
modes.source_chapter: 致菲德尔·卡斯特罗的告别信 (1965)；《玻利维亚日记》(1966-67)；《致儿女的信》；1964年联合国大会演说
modes.key_quote_zh: 让我们面对现实，让我们忠于理想——现实会变，理想是丈量现实的尺子。
modes.key_quote_en: Let us face reality; let us be true to the ideal—reality will change; the ideal is the measure of reality.
process_zh: 定义理想的十年形态：先写清『若理想活着，十年后世界应当是什么样』，作为所有岔口裁决的参照系
岔口全代价核算：把每个选项的全部代价（安全、职位、关系、生命）与理想的存活率并排列出，禁止只算成功收益
拒绝半额投入：识别『既想要理想又想保留退路』的方案，因其会让执行变形，宁选全额押注
知情固执的底线检查：每月用日记对照现实与理想，确认坚持仍在为理想存活率服务而非为自尊服务——固执必须通过定期审计
process_en: Define the ideal's ten-year form: write plainly what the world should look like in ten years if the ideal lives—this is the reference frame for every fork
Full-cost accounting at the fork: list each option's complete price (safety, office, relations, life) beside the ideal's survival odds; tallying only the upside is forbidden
Refuse half-investment: identify schemes that want the ideal while keeping an escape hatch—such schemes deform execution; prefer the full stake

Baseline check for informed obstinacy: use the monthly diary to compare reality against the ideal, confirming the persistence still serves the ideal's survival and not self-esteem—obstinacy must pass periodic audits
representative_cases_zh: 1965年出走：辞去工业部长、放弃古巴国籍、写给卡斯特罗的告别信公开其决裂式选择——在个人声望顶点选择重新成为无名战士
玻利维亚远征：明知成功率极低仍进入，日记显示他对每一步风险的清醒记录——这是『知情之下的价值裁决』而非侥幸冒险
被俘时刻 (1967.10.8)：被俘后拒绝合作、对审讯军官直言，次日就义——终局行为与终身原则一致，遗言要求『告诉菲德尔』
反例警示：终局算法不可被组织简单模仿——追随者以同等方式消耗生命并无制度补偿；把个人殉道标准写进组织KPI是灾难，价值裁决应保留在个人选择层
representative_cases_en: The 1965 departure: resigning the industries ministry, renouncing Cuban citizenship, a farewell letter to Castro making the break public—choosing at the peak of prestige to become a nameless soldier again
The Bolivia expedition: entering while knowing the odds were minuscule, the diary recording each step's risk with lucidity—an informed value-verdict, not a gambler's dash

The moment of capture (Oct 8, 1967): refusing cooperation when taken, speaking plainly to the interrogating officer, executed the next day—the endgame consistent with the lifelong principle, last words asking 'tell Fidel'

Counter-case: the endgame algorithm cannot be copied wholesale by organizations—followers spending their lives the same way receive no institutional compensation; writing personal martyrdom standards into an organization's KPIs is disaster—value-verdicts must remain at the level of personal choice
modern_applications_zh: 创始人抉择：面对高估值收购与使命延续的冲突，以『十年后使命是否还活着』为唯一标准，接受短期损失
科研选题：把个人最贵的资源（十年时间）押在真问题上而非易发表问题上，用终局标准过滤热点诱惑
个人生涯：每个重大跳槽/转型用『理想存活率』而非『短期回报率』裁决，并为此支付可承受的确定代价
组织设计：为愿意做长期价值选择的成员保留『低指标高使命』赛道，但不把殉道标准强加给所有人
modern_applications_en: Founder decisions: facing a rich acquisition against mission continuity, take 'will the mission be alive in ten years' as the sole standard and accept the short-term loss
Research choices: stake your dearest resource—ten years—on true problems rather than publishable ones, filtering fashionable temptations by the endgame standard
Personal career: judge every major move by the ideal's survival odds, not the short-term return, paying a bounded, certain price for it
Organizational design: keep a 'low-metric, high-mission' track for members who choose long-term value—but never impose martyr standards on everyone
